name: 第一旭 熊野店 (Daiichi Asahi Kumano-ten)

claims.text: The bowls are seasoned with a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare in the Kyoto chuka-soba style; standard shoyu is wheat-based, so the broth should be treated as containing wheat.
The kitchen is built around a pork-bone broth, pork chashu and pork gyoza; there is no separate vegetable preparation, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: 福仙楼 北白川店 (Fukusenro Kitashirakawa-ten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are the base of every bowl and are boiled in shared water; there is no gluten-free noodle or separate-pot option mentioned.
The broth is a pork-bone/chicken base finished with a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare; Japanese soy sauce is typically brewed with wheat, so the soup itself is not gluten-free.
All bowls are built on animal stock (pork bone, chicken, back fat) with pork and tendon toppings; no vegan or vegetable broth is offered, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.
Wheat ramen noodles are the base of every bowl, sourced from noodle maker Menya Teigaku (麺屋棣鄂); shared noodle-boiling water means heavy gluten cross-contact throughout the kitchen.
The lineup includes 濃厚醤油とりとんこつ (rich soy chicken-pork-bone) and a 背脂醤油 mazesoba, indicating wheat-based soy tare is used in the broths/seasoning.
All bowls are chicken-and-pork-bone based, with niboshi (dried sardine), pork chashu, back-fat and karaage on the menu; there is no plant-based preparation line.
No allergy information is provided by the shop or in available write-ups.

name: 元祖らーめん大栄 (Ganso Ramen Daiei)

claims.text: Bowls are built on wheat ramen noodles plus a soy-based tare; the shop and broth are not designed around gluten avoidance, so cross-contamination from shared pots and noodle water should be assumed.
The signature is a shoyu (soy sauce) tonkotsu broth; Japanese soy sauce almost always contains wheat, so the tare should be treated as wheat-containing.
All bowls use a pork-and-bone broth and pork chashu; there is no vegan/vegetarian preparation, so no vegan-safe option exists.

The broth is made only from premium pork and bones with no additives or muddiness, so ingredients are simple and transparent; toppings like Kujo negi, mung bean sprouts, and chashu are clearly identifiable.

name: 極太清流らーめん (Gokuboso Seiryu Ramen)

claims.text: Bowls are dressed with a sweet soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in this style is wheat-containing; combined with the wheat noodles there is no celiac-safe path here.
Bowls are built on pork and meat toppings with an animal-based broth; no vegan preparation is mentioned.
Dandan-noodle tare is conventionally built on wheat-based soy sauce and miso; no wheat-free tare is indicated.
Bowls are built around ground pork and char siu and share a meat-based sauce; no plant-based separation is offered.

name: ぎょうざ処 高辻 亮昌 本店 (Gyoza-dokoro Takatsuji Sukemasa Honten)

claims.text: 餃子専門店であり、すべての主力商品が小麦の皮を使用するため、厨房は小麦が常用される環境です。グルテンフリー対応・分離調理に関する記載は確認できませんでした。
和だしと味噌をベースにしたたれや調味料を使用しており、醤油・味噌など小麦を含みうる発酵調味料が用いられている可能性があります。具体的な原材料の公開情報は確認できませんでした。
京もち豚のミンチや鰹だしを中核に使用する肉餃子の専門店で、植物性メニューの分離・専用調理に関する情報は確認できませんでした。
英語メニューを用意しており、にんにく不使用の餃子のため、にんにくを避けたい人には案内しやすい。

name: 博多長浜ラーメン みよし (Hakata Nagahama Ramen Miyoshi)

claims.text: Core menu is wheat ramen noodles in a shared tonkotsu broth with kaedama (noodle refills), so a single shared noodle/broth workflow — high cross-contamination risk for gluten.
The shop is built on a continuously simmered pork-bone broth; there is no separate non-animal broth, so all bowls share an animal-based base.
